issues.description: The solution's data section declares the framebuffer as 'screen_buffer' (section .bss) but the code in the solution references 'display_start'. This name mismatch makes references to 'display_start' undefined in the solution and will cause a linkage/compilation error. The problem statement and the template both refer to the framebuffer label as 'display_start', so the solution's declaration is inconsistent with both the specification and the template.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the framebuffer label consistent. Either rename the .bss declaration in the solution from 'screen_buffer' to 'display_start' or change all code references to use 'screen_buffer'. Prefer using 'display_start' to match the template and problem statement so students see a consistent name across artifacts.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template refer to the screen memory base as the symbol display_start, but the solution's .bss section declares the buffer as screen_buffer while other places in the solution still reference display_start. This inconsistent identifier usage for the same conceptual entity (the display pixel buffer base address) creates unnecessary confusion: students expecting the symbol display_start (as per the problem and template) will not find a matching declaration in the solution, and the mixed usage in the solution itself is likely an unintentional oversight.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the buffer symbol consistent across all artifacts. Either rename the declaration in solution/pixel.asm from 'screen_buffer RESB 8294400' to 'display_start RESB 8294400', or update all references in the solution to use 'screen_buffer' and adjust the problem statement/template to match. Prefer using 'display_start' to remain consistent with the problem and provided template.
